Hi Lydia — great to hear the team is ready to move forward. Short answers up front, then a suggested path: 

- Term: We support 12- and 36-month private offers. Pricing generally improves for multi-year commits; typical delta is 10–18% off list depending on committed spend. For pilot/POC we usually recommend 12 months with an initial usage band and an option to extend.
- Buyer approvals: AWS requires the buyer to accept the private offer in their console and then complete the purchase with a PO (if your finance uses a PO workflow). From experience, enterprise customers usually require: corporate procurement sign-off + BU cost center approval if the contract is above your BU threshold. That’s on Aurelia’s side; on our side we need the signed PO and the private offer acceptance record from AWS to activate.

Suggested activation path (minimal friction):
1) Redwood to generate private offer draft and pricing (we’ll set 12-month pilot pricing: 15% off list for first $X usage).
2) Aurelia legal reviews terms; procurement returns signed PO (scan).
3) Redwood ops (Vanessa) creates the private offer in AWS and shares the offer ID with Aurelia.
4) Aurelia buyer accepts the offer in Marketplace and submits PO to Redwood for invoicing.
5) Redwood confirms activation and shares entitlement/usage dashboards.

I’ve CC’d Vanessa from Marketplace Ops to outline the AWS-side steps and any metadata we’ll need from your finance team (Seller ID, AWS account ID, billing alias). Attached is a draft PO-friendly term sheet for your legal to review.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the steps with procurement.

—Jonas

Hi Lydia, Jonas — jumping in from Marketplace Ops. I’ll own the private-offer creation and activation steps. Practical checklist + items we’ll need from Aurelia: 

1) Buyer info we need from Aurelia (send in one email to ops@redwood.com):
   - Buyer AWS Account ID (12-digit)
   - Buyer email that will accept the private offer (usually procurement alias)
   - Full legal entity name for the PO (matches tax/billing records)

2) Offer metadata + how we configure it:
   - Term: we can set 12 or 36 months; for a pilot choose 12 with an auto-extension option.
   - Pricing bands: we’ll include a baseline unit price and optional volume tiers; for a pilot I suggest a fixed-rate band for first 6 months to simplify approvals.
   - Seller ID and listing: I’ll map the private offer to the existing Redwood listing (we’ll provide Offer ID).

3) Typical delays and gating:
   - Buyer acceptance in AWS console can be instantaneous but often stalls if the BU approver is not the procurement contact. Make sure the person accepting the offer has the necessary permissions.
   - If Aurelia requires a signed master services agreement before PO, that adds legal time — we can sign the PO-facing term sheet and then add an MSA later if needed.

Next steps from Ops (what I’ll do):
- Prepare private offer draft once I have the buyer AWS ID and PO contact.
- Share AWS Offer ID and DocuSign link for PO/term acceptance if Aurelia needs electronic signature.
- Coordinate with Billing to ensure invoices map to the PO number.

Jonas — I attached the internal activation checklist and a sample private offer payload we push to AWS (redacted). Lydia — if you can send the buyer account ID and confirm the procurement alias, I’ll draft the offer today.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
